note: Three hand-authored personas for the Agile Principles Assessment maturity engine. calculateMaturity(data) takes the full assessment shape ({ respondent, responses: [12 x {score,comment,weight}], actionPlan }) - responses[i] corresponds to PRINCIPLES[i] positionally (1-indexed principle number = i+1). clampWeight coerces a missing/zero/negative/NaN weight to 1.0 and clamps the valid range to [0.5, 2.0] BEFORE it is used in the weighted mean - a weight of 0.3 in the input becomes 0.5 in weightedSum, and 2.5 becomes 2.0; weightsCustomised is true whenever any principle's clamped weight differs from 1.0 by more than 1e-6, including a clamped-but-not-exactly-1 weight. meanScore/weightedMeanScore are null (and maturity 'insufficient-data') unless at least 6 of the 12 principles have a non-null score; below that floor the weightedMeanScore band thresholds never apply no matter how good or bad the answered principles look. Per-principle flags fire independently of the band: any score <= 2 raises that principle's own FLAG_SPECS entry (flagId F-<CATEGORY>, category/priority fixed per principle), and a score of EXACTLY 1 additionally raises F-CRITICAL-P<NN> right after it - both checks run per principle in PRINCIPLES order, so the two flags for the same principle are adjacent, not grouped by type. additionalFlags are folded into the result (push order, not sorted by priority). Regenerate 'expected' with: bin/test-personas agile-principles-assessment --update

personas.name: Optimising organisation - every principle scored 5/5
personas.description: All 12 principles scored 5 with the default weight 1.0 (weightsCustomised false). Expect answeredCount 12, meanScore 5, weightedMeanScore 5, maturity 'optimising' (>=4.5), twelve R-Pxx-HIGH fired rules in principle order, and no flags at all (no score <= 2 anywhere).

firedRules.description: Customer feedback loops are tight; keep tracking outcome metrics, not output.
Change is treated as an opportunity; preserve light-weight change-control overhead.
Releases are routine and low-drama. Continue to shrink batch size where possible.
Daily collaboration is healthy; safeguard the rituals that keep stakeholders close to the work.
People feel trusted and supported. Continue investing in autonomy and tools.
Real-time conversation is the default for important decisions; document outcomes, not deliberations.
Progress is measured by shipped, working capability. Continue.
Pace is sustainable. Watch for early signs of crunch creeping in.
Technical health is part of definition-of-done; keep refactoring continuous.
Scope is actively trimmed; resist gold-plating.
Teams choose how to deliver. Reinforce psychological safety to keep emergence working.
Retrospectives drive concrete experiments. Continue closing the loop on each.

personas.name: Partially answered with custom weights - developing, three non-critical flags
personas.description: Non-critical edge case exercising weight clamping and the answered-floor arithmetic together. Only principles 1-8 are scored (9-12 left null); weights of 0.3 and 2.5 are supplied on P4 and P6 to demonstrate clamping to [0.5, 2.0]. Scores: P1=4(w1.5) P2=2(w1) P3=5(w1) P4=2(w0.3->0.5) P5=3(w1) P6=4(w2.5->2.0) P7=3(w1) P8=2(w1). sum=25, answeredCount=8 (>=6, reportable). meanScore = round2(25/8) = 3.13. weightedSum = 4x1.5 + 2x1 + 5x1 + 2x0.5 + 3x1 + 4x2 + 3x1 + 2x1 = 30; weightSum = 1.5+1+1+0.5+1+2+1+1 = 9; weightedMeanScore = round2(30/9) = 3.33 -> maturity 'developing' (>=3.0, <3.75). weightsCustomised true. Fired rules: R-P01-HIGH, R-P02-LOW, R-P03-HIGH, R-P04-LOW, R-P05-MID, R-P06-HIGH, R-P07-MID, R-P08-LOW, then R-P09..R-P12-UNANSWERED. Flags in principle order: F-CHANGE-RESISTANCE (P2, score 2), F-SILO-COLLABORATION (P4, score 2), F-BURNOUT-RISK (P8, score 2) - no F-CRITICAL-Pxx (no score is exactly 1), no F-INSUFFICIENT-DATA (8 >= 6).

personas.name: Critical - every principle scored 1 or 2, seven at the critical floor
personas.description: Critical/highest-severity persona. All 12 principles answered, alternating score 1 and 2 (P1,P2,P4,P6,P8,P10,P12 = 1; P3,P5,P7,P9,P11 = 2), default weight throughout (weightsCustomised false). sum = 7x1 + 5x2 = 17; meanScore = weightedMeanScore = round2(17/12) = 1.42 -> maturity 'ad-hoc' (<2.0). All twelve perPrincipleBands are 'low' (both 1 and 2 fall below the mid threshold of exactly 3), so firedRules is R-P01-LOW through R-P12-LOW. Every principle's own FLAG_SPECS flag fires (all scores <=2): F-CUSTOMER-DISCONNECT, F-CHANGE-RESISTANCE, F-SLOW-DELIVERY, F-SILO-COLLABORATION, F-MORALE-RISK, F-COMMUNICATION-GAP, F-OUTPUT-NOT-OUTCOME, F-BURNOUT-RISK, F-TECHNICAL-DEBT, F-OVER-ENGINEERING, F-COMMAND-AND-CONTROL, F-NO-RETROSPECTIVE - and the seven principles scored exactly 1 each additionally raise F-CRITICAL-P<NN> immediately after their own flag (interleaved by principle, not grouped): F-CRITICAL-P01, F-CRITICAL-P02, F-CRITICAL-P04, F-CRITICAL-P06, F-CRITICAL-P08, F-CRITICAL-P10, F-CRITICAL-P12 - 19 flags total. No F-INSUFFICIENT-DATA (12 >= 6).

firedRules.description: Customer is at arm's length. Establish a recurring feedback loop with real users this quarter.
Change is treated as a threat. Replace heavy change-control with a lightweight backlog re-ordering ritual.
Delivery is rare or unpredictable. Reduce batch size and remove release ceremonies that add no value.
Stakeholders and engineers are working in silos. Co-locate decisions or create a daily 15-minute joint stand-up.
Morale is low or trust is thin. Address environment, tooling, or management style before adding more process.
Important decisions are stuck in chat or email. Establish a synchronous decision ritual.
Progress is reported by activity, not by working software. Make working software the headline metric.
Crunch and heroics are routine. Reset capacity and protect non-overtime delivery before scope.
Technical debt is accumulating faster than it is being repaid. Treat this as the top organisational risk.
Over-engineering or scope creep is the norm. Make trimming a non-optional part of planning.
Command-and-control culture. Push architecture and design decisions back to the team and provide context, not directives.
Retrospectives are skipped or theatrical. Reinstate them on a fixed schedule with one written follow-up.
